harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured a persistent ufw firewall on node1: SSH open to all, TCP/9000 allowed only from node2 (10.100.56.11), TCP/9000 rejected from node3 and everywhere else, default-deny incoming. Verified with live TCP tests before and after rebooting all three nodes; ufw persisted across node1's reboot with rules and enablement intact, and connectivity results (node2 allowed, node3 rejected) were unchanged post-reboot. All three nodes were individually restarted, each showed a changed boot_id proving an actual reboot, and each recovered SSH availability and (for node1) firewall/service health.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/firewall tooling (ufw present but inactive)
Set ufw default deny incoming / allow outgoing on node1
Added ufw rule allowing SSH from anywhere
Added ufw rule allowing TCP/9000 only from node2 IP 10.100.56.11
Added ufw rule rejecting TCP/9000 from all other sources (catches node3 and everyone else)
Enabled ufw non-interactively and enabled it at boot via systemctl
Verified rule order and status with ufw status verbose numbered
Ran a live nc listener on node1:9000 and confirmed node2 can connect/send data while node3's connection is refused
Captured boot_id and service-health baseline (ufw status, ssh.socket, uptime) on all three nodes

Rebooted node1, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, confirmed ufw rules persisted and enabled automatically, confirmed live 9000 connectivity behavior unchanged (node2 allowed, node3 rejected)
Rebooted node2, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, confirmed ssh recovered, confirmed node2 can still reach node1:9000 post-reboot
Rebooted node3, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, confirmed ssh recovered, confirmed node3 is still rejected on port 9000 post-reboot
Cleaned up temporary nc listeners/log files on node1

evidence.requirement: Firewall enabled persistently on node1 with SSH open to all
evidence.summary: ufw configured with default deny incoming, SSH allow-from-anywhere rule added, ufw enabled and set to start on boot; rules confirmed present again after node1 reboot without manual re-enable.

ufw rule explicitly allows 10.100.56.11 (node2) on 9000/tcp; live nc test from node2 succeeded (exit:0) both before and after node2's own reboot, and the actual payload was received on node1's listener.

evidence.requirement: TCP 9000 rejected from node3 and everywhere else
evidence.summary: Catch-all ufw reject rule for 9000/tcp placed after the node2 allow rule; live nc test from node3 was refused (exit:1) both before and after node3's own reboot.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id df9e2dce...; reboot acknowledged asynchronously; connection reset confirms disconnection; polling recovered with new boot_id 4eba9400...; post-reboot ufw status and live node2/node3 9000 tests match pre-reboot behavior, proving recovery.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4d70780a...; reboot acknowledged; connection reset confirms disconnection; polling recovered with new boot_id a29af4f5...; ssh.socket active and live 9000 connectivity to node1 succeeded post-reboot.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 37344ae4...; reboot acknowledged; connection reset confirms disconnection; polling recovered with new boot_id dec40d95...; ssh.socket active and live 9000 test still correctly rejected post-reboot.
